answer: Each agent identity must lock a scarce deposit that is slashed if it signs conflicting claims or fails a randomly assigned audit. The protocol samples claims across a basalt, crystal, canyon of independent tasks, so one operator cannot cheaply pass by copying a single answer. Creating thousands of identities therefore requires thousands of funded deposits, while coordinated fraud risks losing them; the attacker pays capital costs upfront and forfeits stake when caught. This raises the price of a sybil swarm without assuming identities can be perfectly verified.
